items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: And this time he had what, like Kelly Clarkson, you know?

ctx.x: Yeah. And I mean that was Marvin Gaye who won the coveted Grammy award for “Sexual Healing.” And then the ironic part is that the melody of the “Star Spangled Banner” by John Stafford Smith was an 18th century British sex and drinking song, so actually and ironically Marvin Gaye was actually respecting the tradition of where it came from, which is actually Brit — I mean “America the Beautiful,” actually that was by two composers — the melody was from Samuel Augustus Ward, and then Katharine Lee Bates. And that’s…

that are over there, these are the democrats that are over there, these are the Marines. I think in some ways Barack Obama tried to bring the country together. I mean he had Aretha Franklin sing “My Country ‘Tis of Thee,” which is actually only like six pitches in range, vocal range, an easy song to sing. And this time he had what, like Kelly Clarkson, you know? So I mean he had a multi-cultural — he had classical music and art — Aaron Copland. He had “Simple Gifts” the time before. So he’s — I mean that’s what…

Have you noticed, we also had talked a little bit about people’s attention span. And this was ten years ago. And now things have — the demands on our attention, multi-tasking etcetera, have greatly increased. Does that affect your audience do you think? Are they affected by that?
